skill.name: dispatching-parallel-agents
skill.description: Guide for splitting independent coding failures into focused tasks for parallel AI agents and safely integrating their results.
skill.summary: Coordinate independent debugging or test-fix work across parallel AI agents.

content.value_statement: Sequential debugging slows teams when failures are independent. This skill shows how to split focused tasks across parallel AI agents and integrate results safely.
actual_capabilities: Identifies when coding failures are independent enough for parallel agent work.
Shows how to scope one agent task per test file or subsystem.
Provides a prompt structure with goals, constraints, and expected output.
Explains how to review agent summaries before integrating changes.
Recommends full test verification after parallel fixes return.
limitations: It is guidance documentation, not an executable orchestration tool.
It assumes the user can launch agents in their chosen AI environment.
It is unsuitable when failures share state or require full-system context.
It does not resolve merge conflicts or verify code changes automatically.

use_cases.title: Split Independent Test Failures
use_cases.description: Assign separate failing test files to parallel agents, then review each root-cause summary before integration.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Refactor Cleanup
use_cases.description: Separate unrelated post-refactor defects by subsystem and give each agent a narrow repair scope.

use_cases.title: Speed Up Bug Triage
use_cases.description: Use focused agent prompts to investigate unrelated bug reports without waiting for one investigation to finish.

prompt_templates.title: Find Parallel Work
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these failures and group them by independent problem domain. Tell me which tasks can run in parallel and which need shared context.

prompt_templates.title: Create Agent Tasks
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare scoped prompts for separate agents.
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn these independent failure groups into focused agent prompts. Include the scope, goal, constraints, and expected summary for each agent.

prompt_templates.title: Review Returned Fixes
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare these agent summaries and changed areas. Identify conflicts, missing verification, and the safest order for integrating the fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Multi-Agent Debugging
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced coordination across a larger codebase.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a parallel debugging plan for these failing suites. Define agent boundaries, shared-state risks, verification steps, and integration checkpoints.

output_examples.input: Three unrelated test files fail after a refactor.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends one focused agent per test file, with clear constraints and a required summary of root cause and changes.

output_examples.input: Two failures may share the same underlying production bug.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends investigating them together first, because a single fix may affect both results.

output_examples.input: Parallel agents return changes touching nearby files.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends reviewing summaries, checking conflicts, running the full suite, and spot checking the integrated result.

best_practices: Dispatch agents only when each task has a clear independent scope.
Give every agent the needed context, constraints, and expected summary.
Review all returned changes together before running final verification.
anti_patterns: Sending one broad request that asks an agent to fix every failure.
Dispatching parallel agents when failures likely share the same root cause.
Accepting agent changes without checking conflicts or running the full suite.

faq.question: What does this skill help me do?
faq.answer: It helps you divide independent coding problems across parallel AI agents and integrate their results carefully.

faq.question: Does it run agents automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides a workflow and prompt structure for tools like Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: When should I avoid this skill?
faq.answer: Avoid it when failures are related, need shared context, or require agents to edit the same files.

faq.question: Can it help with test failures?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples focus on grouping failing test files and assigning each independent group to a focused agent.

faq.question: How should agents report back?
faq.answer: Ask each agent for the root cause, changed areas, verification performed, and any remaining risks.

faq.question: Is this skill specific to Claude Code?
faq.answer: No. It can guide parallel task delegation in Claude, Codex, Claude Code, or similar AI coding environments.
